skill.name: camera-prompt-quickcheck
skill.description: Check camera directions before submitting prompts to Runway, Kling, Sora, Veo, or Seedance. A local Python linter flags ambiguous movement, conflicting directions, and missing framing or pacing details.
skill.summary: Score AI video camera prompts and get specific suggestions for motion, framing, and the final shot.

security_audit.summary: All 24 static matches are false positives: the backticks are Markdown formatting, and the reconnaissance match is camera-pacing advice. The documented invocation risks command injection if an agent substitutes raw prompt text into a shell command. The report also echoes untrusted prompt text, which downstream agents or Markdown renderers must handle as data.

remediation.issue: The agent workflow shows a shell command with a user prompt placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the shell template with a direct argument-vector example that passes the prompt as data and explicitly disables shell execution.

remediation.issue: Reports echo untrusted prompt text, and the Markdown formatter does not escape it.
remediation.suggestion: Omit the prompt from default reports, escape it when displayed in Markdown, and instruct downstream consumers to treat any echoed text as data.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Shell Template for User Prompts
semantic_findings.description: The agent workflow shows a shell command with a double-quoted user prompt placeholder. An agent that substitutes raw text into the command can let the shell interpret user input and execute unintended commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow places untrusted prompt text inside shell source without prescribing safe argument passing. The risk requires an agent to interpolate the text and invoke a shell.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Prompt Text Echoed Into Agent Reports
semantic_findings.description: The Markdown report encloses the original prompt in fixed backticks without escaping it, so input can break the intended code span. Downstream agents that treat echoed prompt text as instructions can be misled.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The formatter directly inserts the normalized prompt into Markdown, and JSON also retains the prompt as data. Following echoed instructions would require unsafe downstream handling.

content.user_title: Check Camera Directions in AI Video Prompts
content.value_statement: Vague camera directions can lead to unwanted movement or framing in generated video. Check each shot prompt locally and get specific suggestions before spending generation credits.
actual_capabilities: Recognize common directions such as dolly, pan, tilt, orbit, and a static shot.
Flag ambiguous zoom wording, unlabeled dolly and zoom combinations, or three or more competing movement axes.
Flag vague style words without pacing cues and moving shots without a speed description.
Check for starting framing or a subject or horizon anchor, plus a final hold or reveal.
Return a score out of 100, rule IDs, deductions, and suggested edits.
Run locally with the Python standard library and print Markdown or JSON.
limitations: It matches text patterns, so it can miss synonyms, negation, or the intended order of moves.
It recognizes some Chinese phrases but does not provide comprehensive multilingual analysis.
It does not render video, inspect images, or predict how a particular generator will interpret a prompt.
It suggests edits but does not automatically rewrite full shots or create keyframes.

use_cases.title: Clarify a product reveal
use_cases.description: Check whether a product shot specifies a camera move, keeps the product in frame, and ends on a clear hold.

use_cases.title: Review camera notes before handoff
use_cases.description: Find conflicting moves and unclear zoom wording before sending individual shot descriptions to a generation operator.

use_cases.title: Add a local prompt quality check
use_cases.description: Use the structured report to record rule IDs and scores in a prompt review pipeline without calling a generation service.

prompt_templates.title: Check a first draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this shot prompt: [shot prompt]. Show the score, the two largest deductions, and one small edit for each.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review one draft before generating a clip.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a zoom or dolly
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this prompt: [shot prompt]. I want [physical camera travel or a stationary lens zoom]. Flag wording that conflicts with that intent and suggest a replacement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Make the intended perspective change clear.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two shot revisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [version A] and [version B] separately. Compare scores and rule IDs, then identify whether either version loses the intended subject framing or final hold.
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose between two drafts of the same shot.

prompt_templates.title: Review a batch for a pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Check each numbered shot separately in JSON mode. Pass each prompt as a literal argument without a shell. Summarize scores below 85 and list their rule IDs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review multiple shots before sending them to a generation queue.

output_examples.input: Cinematic epic zoom in on detective face.
output: C01 and C02: Name a camera move and specify whether the camera travels or the lens zooms.
C04, C05, and C06: Add a pace, a framing anchor, and a clear final hold.

output_examples.input: Slow, steady dolly in from a medium shot, keeping the product centered, then settle into a close-up and hold steady.
output: Detected movement: dolly in. No diagnostic deductions.

best_practices: Review one shot at a time so the score reflects the moves intended for that shot.
Specify the main move and its pace, then name the subject framing and the final camera position.
Pass prompt text as a literal argument without shell interpolation and treat any echoed text as data.
anti_patterns: Use broad style words in place of a camera move and a speed description.
Stack three or more camera moves in one shot without separating them.
Treat a passing score as proof that a video generator will follow the shot directions.

faq.question: What do I need to run the linter?
faq.answer: You need Python 3. The script uses the standard library and does not require an API key or internet connection.

faq.question: Does it send my prompt to a video service?
faq.answer: No. The Python script checks the text locally and does not submit it to a video service.

faq.question: What score counts as a pass?
faq.answer: A score of 85 or higher is a pass. Below 85, review the deductions before generating the shot.

faq.question: Can I use the report in an automated workflow?
faq.answer: Yes. JSON mode returns the score, status, and rule findings. Treat the echoed prompt as data.

faq.question: Does the linter allow intentional dolly zooms?
faq.answer: Yes. Label the combined move as a dolly zoom or vertigo effect so it is not flagged as an unlabeled collision.

faq.question: Will it rewrite my prompt for me?
faq.answer: The script suggests targeted changes for each finding. It does not generate a complete rewritten prompt or plan keyframes.
